fields.Text: A UML class box has three sections, top to bottom: {{c1::name}}, {{c2::attributes}}, {{c3::methods}}.

fields.Front: What do - and + before an attribute or method mean in UML?

fields.Back: 'has-a' relationship; e.g., teacher has a student.
'is-a' relationship; e.g., Admin is a type of User.

fields.Front: In the e-commerce class diagram, which classes inherit from User?
In the e-commerce class diagram, what does Customer own by composition, with what multiplicities?
fields.Back: Shopping Cart (1 Customer to 0..* carts) and Orders (1 Customer to 0..* orders).

fields.Front: In the e-commerce class diagram, what does Orders own by composition?
fields.Back: Shipping Info (1 to 1) and Order Details (1 to 1, labelled 'has a').

fields.Front: Multiplicity: plain line with no numbers between A and B means?
fields.Back: One B with each A; one A with each B.

fields.Front: Multiplicity: 1 at A and * at B means?
fields.Back: Zero or more Bs with each A; one A with each B.

fields.Front: Multiplicity: * at both A and B means?
fields.Back: Zero or more Bs with each A, and zero or more As with each B (many-to-many).

fields.Front: Multiplicity: 1 at A and 2..5 at B means?
fields.Back: Two to five Bs with each A; one A with each B.

fields.Front: What does a single arrowhead from A to B with * at B mean?
fields.Back: Zero or more Bs with each A, and B knows nothing about A (navigable only from A to B).

fields.Front: What guidance is given for refining class diagrams?
fields.Back: Iterative design; avoid overcomplicating diagrams; each class should represent a clear, distinct concept.

fields.Text: UML class relationships: association is {{c1::'has-a'}}, inheritance is {{c2::'is-a'}}, composition is {{c3::'strong has-a'}}.
UML notation: a {{c1::solid line}} for association, an {{c2::arrow}} for inheritance, a {{c3::diamond}} for composition.
In UML multiplicity, * alone means {{c1::zero or more}} and 2..5 means {{c2::two to five}}.
